intelligence.essence: No cached artifact, background worker, concurrent writer, or successor may publish or reuse a qualification unless its evidence dependencies are valid at the moment of publication or consequential use. Older evidence can remain in history, but it cannot regain current authority through a delayed write. Three invariants: StaleWriter ⇒ RejectPublication; RevokedEvidence ⇒ NoStaleCertification; IndependentValidSupport ⇒ PreserveSupportedClaim. The first two prevent regression; the third prevents unnecessary intelligence loss. An old worker can finish late, a cache can refresh out of order, a successor can wake from an old checkpoint — but none can turn yesterday's qualification into today's authority. This is a distributed consistency problem, not a cache-expiration problem: a cache may be completely accurate when generated and dangerous by the time it is published.
intelligence.falsifier: A delayed writer's stale REQUALIFIED overwriting a newer SUSPENDED; a fencing-token-less worker regaining publication rights after supersession; a revocation committed without atomic ordering against concurrent publications; a crash between revocation commit and notification restoring eligibility; wall-clock timestamps used as version order; a successor treating an old package PASS as current certification.

human_view.meaning: Imagine two people editing the same document, and one of them is working from yesterday's copy. When they hit save, the system must reject it — yesterday's version doesn't get to overwrite today's. Every claim, every piece of evidence, and every published page gets its own version number from one trusted counter, so 'newer' always means 'based on fresher evidence,' never 'whoever saved last.' Workers get numbered tickets: if your ticket is old, your work is done but it doesn't publish — you rebase onto the current truth first. And if the system crashes halfway through, recovery replays the log without ever resurrecting a dead qualification. The result: nothing from yesterday can sneak back into authority today, no matter how late it arrives.

intelligence.learning_lesson: This is the mechanical guarantee underneath SN-0784's invalidation semantics: policies say what SHOULD happen; compare-and-swap, fencing tokens, and atomic publication make it IMPOSSIBLE for it not to happen. The framework's own gap analysis is the pattern to repeat everywhere: find where version-aware logic exists without transactional enforcement, and close exactly that gap. Version order from the authoritative state, never from local clocks or agent assertions.

intelligence.measurement_contract: Ten concurrency tests: old writer finishes after revocation → rejected; two writers, one projection → only validated revision wins; new writer beats old → old fencing token rejected; evidence revoked mid-generation → cannot publish on obsolete dependencies; notification lost → read-time protection holds, replay refreshes; duplicate revocation delivery → idempotent, no regression; E1 revoked + E2 sufficient → E2 conclusion stays eligible; old successor opened offline → history usable, certification withheld; publication races revocation → atomic ordering wins; worker crashes mid-refresh → reconciliation resumes without overwriting newer state. The decisive experiment: deterministic race — pause writer pre-publication, commit revocation, resume writer → publication MUST fail; same with an unaffected claim → usable without rebuild. Proves protection AND selectivity.

naya_view.directive: Maintain three monotonic version namespaces from the authoritative state. Require atomic compare-and-swap on publication with the full dependency predicate. Issue fencing tokens from the shared authority; reject superseded workers even if their lease hasn't expired. Bind fragments to precise dependency manifests tracking validated support paths. Apply per-surface publication rules. Recover via transactional outbox with idempotent replay and independent reconciliation. Never let notification loss restore eligibility. Never order versions by wall clock.

simple_view.meaning: Yesterday's work can't overwrite today's truth. Version everything from one trusted counter, and check the evidence is still good at the exact moment of publishing.

intelligence.successor_effect: A cold successor inherits the publication discipline: it can read old packages as history but can never promote their qualifications to current authority without revalidation against the authoritative state.
